info.title: OpenConditions
info.description: Road conditions as model records. Collections are paginated by a keyset cursor: a walk is complete when `next` is null. TraFF is instead one complete bounded feed, or 413 when filters must be narrowed. A request without a bearer token reads in the public scope, which withholds restricted sources and licences that are not public; the operator token reads in the operator scope, which withholds nothing. The emitters always read in the public scope.

operatorToken.description: The instance's `OPENCONDITIONS_OPERATOR_TOKEN`: grants the operator scope and skips the rate limiter.

get.summary: A complete public TraFF 0.8 feed from one database snapshot, not paged. No cursor or limit parameters. At most 20,000 candidate situations and 32 MiB of UTF-8 XML; narrow bbox, source or time filters on 413. Vehicle-specific, incomplete and explicitly directional situations without representable travel order are withheld. Missing direction uses TraFF's bidirectional default; times have whole-second UTC precision.

get.summary: Server-sent events: up to 20,000 live matching public situations, then changes (`event: situation`) and removals (`event: remove`). Polls run 15 s after the preceding read/write cycle. Each connection starts a new replacement view; clients must clear that subscription on every successful open, including reconnects. Last-Event-ID is ignored; event IDs identify records, not replay cursors. No initial-completion marker or durable replay; the cap can truncate large results.

get.summary: One situation, tombstoned or not (one past its `freshness.expiresAt` at `at` answers 404), with its evidence, the graph binding of its place (`binding`) and of each effect with a place or a direction of its own (`effectBindings`, by effect id). A binding is `{ status, confidence, directionMode, reason, boundAt }`; routing reads only `exact` and `likely`. `reason` (null when there is none) says why a location was not bound or was kept off routing, e.g. `no_candidates`, `conflicting_direction` (the stated direction contradicts the location; nothing bound) or `direction_undecided` (one direction is stated but the geometry cannot tell which carriageway).

get.summary: Live features as records, one keyset page ordered by id (the limit counts features); `canonical=1` serves one feature per cluster of linked features under its canonical id. Components only with `expand=components`; `expand=latest` adds `latest` (each feature's readings in effect, by feature id) and `expand=offers` adds `offers` (each feature's live offers, by feature id). A reading is `{ property, componentKey?, qualifiers?, result, phenomenonTime, validUntil?, source, provenance, contributors? }`; `provenance` is the captured credit snapshot `{ sourceId, attribution, upstream?, mergedSources?: [{ source, recordId, attribution, upstream? }] }`, containing no reporter, raw references or private evidence; it is independent of feature and catalogue metadata. A fused reading lists the sources it was fused from in `contributors`. The operator reads `@fused`, the fusion of every source; the public scope reads a fusion of public sources only: `@fused` when every contributor is public, else `@fused-public`, and none when no contributor is public. A read with `bbox` and a kind, property or domain an on-demand source produces, of the records this route lists, first fetches that source's stale grid cells inside its coverage, within its request limits, waiting up to `OPENCONDITIONS_ON_DEMAND_DEADLINE_MS` (default 3000); the response then carries `coverage: { partial, sources: [{ id, complete, reason? }] }`, `reason` one of `too_many_cells`, `limited`, `failed`, `deadline` or `missing_configuration`. `partial` is true when a source that could answer fell short; a source missing its configuration is listed with its reason but does not make the answer partial. A partial answer is not cached. A read without `bbox`, or for a past `at`, never fetches; `source` limits the sources fetched.

get.summary: The feeds this instance serves, by id: name, source format (`format`) and `qualifier` where the feed has one, licence (`license`, the permission policy ID, and `licensing`, captured scoped definitions and notices), attribution, homepage, terms (url, review date and note), the `notice` the publisher requires to accompany any display of its data, rights, and coverage (the ISO 3166 `countries` a feed covers, or the `bbox` an on-demand feed answers for; a global one covers the world), for crediting and disclosing them and for knowing which areas a feed stands for. A camera feed whose stills a consumer may proxy lists their hosts in `imageHosts` (an exact host, `*.domain`, or `host/path/`). Catalogue children are credited through their parent; disabled feeds are left out. A restricted feed is listed and marked `restricted` (its records are withheld from the public scope, the entry is metadata). The list is the same in both scopes; `scope` (`public` or `operator`) names the scope the request was served in, so a consumer knows whether the restricted feeds' records reach it. `crowd` credits the instance's crowd reports, which are no feed: `{ id: "crowd", name, license, licensing, url?, rights }`, for the readings and contributor lists naming the source `crowd` (crowd readings stay on the instance that landed them; a crowd record, a federated one included, carries its own credit in `provenance.attribution`).
